summary: The B03X is Leapmotor's smallest SUV and, at $26,990 before on-road costs for the Style ($29,990 drive-away on launch offer), one of the cheapest electric SUVs in Australia, sold in two front-drive grades: the 39.8kWh Style and the 53kWh Design LR at $30,990. It reached dealers as a pre-order in late 2026, so the only Australian verdicts so far are international first drives from CarExpert, CarsGuide and Chasing Cars, which agree it is roomy, well equipped and efficient for the money. They split on how much the dynamics matter: CarExpert rated it very good overall, while Chasing Cars found the light, slow steering, loose rear end and nagging driver-assist alerts left it with little appeal to keen drivers.
pros: The $26,990 Style undercuts the BYD Atto 2 Dynamic ($31,990) by $5,000 before on-roads and comes within $500 of the Geely EX2, while being a 4.27m SUV with a 475L boot
Bigger boot than its price rivals: 475L seats up and 1,315L folded on Leapmotor's Australian figures, plus a 105L waterproof underfloor bin, against about 380L for the Atto 2 and 375L for the EX2
The Design LR's 53kWh LFP pack gives 382km WLTP and 133kW DC charging (30-80% in about 16 minutes), with heated seats and wheel, power driver's seat and 360-degree camera for $30,990
Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, a 14.6-inch screen, seven airbags and a full driver-assist suite on both grades, plus an eight-year/160,000km battery warranty
cons: Not rated to tow at launch; CarExpert says a towbar and rating are planned for a later model year
No ANCAP rating yet (testing expected in early 2027), and the B05's five stars do not carry over
Light, slow steering and intrusive speed-warning and lane-keep alerts that reset each drive, with near-total reliance on the touchscreen and no physical climate buttons
The Style's 39.8kWh pack manages only 292km WLTP on 18-inch steel wheels, about 50km short of a base Atto 2, and DC charging tops out at 100kW
Six-year/150,000km vehicle warranty trails the seven years from Kia, MG and GWM, and Leapmotor's thin dealer network and campaign pricing point to weak resale
